source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: SET-BC
entries.description: A provincial outreach program of the B.C. Ministry of Education and Child Care, hosted by the Vancouver School Board, that loans assistive technology to school districts and trains and supports school teams working with students with disabilities or complex needs. Families do not apply directly: requests go through the SET-BC district partner in the student's school district.
entries.cost_note: The FAQ says there is no cost to use SET-BC's website, resources or training modules; equipment is loaned to schools, not sold.
entries.evidence: Since 1989, SET-BC has provided BC students, classrooms, schools, and districts with the services, technology, and support needed to better educate students with complex needs.
entries.notes: CNAF lists SET-BC twice ('Special Education Index' and 'Special Education Technology (SET) B.C.'), both linking to setbc.org. The FAQ says all services must be requested through a SET-BC District Partner and SET-BC does not deal directly with schools, teachers or parents. Phone and email from the home and About Us pages.

entries.name: Disability funding for post-secondary students (StudentAid BC)
entries.description: StudentAid BC, the B.C. government's student financial aid service, has extra funding for college and university students with a permanent, or persistent or prolonged, disability. Once StudentAid BC confirms a student's disability status, the student may get non-repayable grants and bursaries, money for services and equipment, and full-time funding while taking a reduced course load.
entries.cost_note: The page describes non-repayable grant and bursary funding for eligible students (alongside student loans).
entries.evidence: There are programs available to help students with disabilities pay for extra costs during college or university.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the StudentAid BC home page, an old permanent-disability help page and application PDF (both now 404), the form library, and the B.C. supplemental bursary at an old address (404); that bursary is now at https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships/bc-supplemental-bursary-students-disabilities ($800 a year full-time, $400 part-time, B.C. public schools only). A medical assessment is needed to verify the disability, and the application process is moving to a new system in 2026. Phone and email from the Contact Information page.

entries.name: Learning Disability Assessment Bursary (StudentAid BC)
entries.description: A StudentAid BC bursary of up to $3,500 toward the cost of a learning disability assessment for college or university students. It is for students who qualify for StudentAid BC funding, take post-secondary courses at a designated B.C. public school, and have been recommended for an assessment by their school's accessibility services office.
entries.cost_note: A bursary of up to $3,500 toward the up-front cost of the assessment.
entries.evidence: This bursary program helps part-time or full-time students with the up-front costs of the learning disabilities assessment.
entries.notes: Students apply through the accessibility services office at their post-secondary school. Phone and email from StudentAid BC's Contact Information page.

entries.name: RelatedMinds Psychological Services (Dr. Jim Roche)
entries.description: The private practice of Dr. Jim Roche, a licensed psychologist who does autism, ADHD and psychoeducational assessments for adolescents and adults. He also offers cognitive behavioural and narrative therapy and parent consultations about behaviour, in person or by video or phone.
entries.cost_note: Therapy is $260 per hour.
entries.evidence: My practice is focused on diagnostic assessments and treatment for ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorder, and Specific Learning Disabilities, including psychoeducational assessments.
entries.notes: CNAF links to relatedminds.com, which now redirects to relatedmindsbc.squarespace.com. The site says his schedule is full until about December 10 and that first contact is best by email; that address is a personal Gmail, so it is left out. The practice is at the Production Way SkyTrain station (his Psychology Today link says Burnaby) and his contact and mailing addresses are in Vancouver.

entries.name: Pacific Autism Family Network (PAFN)
entries.description: A B.C. charity for autistic and neurodivergent people and their families, with a centre in Richmond and local spokes in Chilliwack and Prince George. The Richmond centre houses clinics, programs and partner services, and the spokes run free community programs and help families find their way through the autism diagnosis and funding process.
entries.cost_note: Spoke programs in Chilliwack and Prince George are described as free; costs for clinic and partner services are not given on these pages.
entries.evidence: Pacific Autism Family Network (PAFN) is a network of support for Autistic and otherwise neurodivergent individuals and their families.
entries.notes: CNAF lists it as the Pacific Autism Family Centre (then a planned centre); it is now the Pacific Autism Family Network, and pacificautismfamily.com redirects to www.pacificautismfamily.com. Spokes: Chilliwack 778-704-0060, Prince George 250-645-0995. PAFN also administers AIDE Canada (national entry in this file). Contact details from the Contact page.

entries.name: BC Autism Assessment Network (BCAAN)
entries.description: B.C.'s public autism assessment program, based at Sunny Hill Health Centre at BC Children's Hospital with regional assessment centres. It assesses and diagnoses children and youth up to their 19th birthday who are referred by a pediatrician, psychiatrist or nurse practitioner.
entries.cost_note: The B.C. government's autism diagnosis page says BCAAN provides free diagnostic assessments for children up to age 19.
entries.evidence: The BC Autism Assessment Network (BCAAN) at Sunny Hill Health Centre provides assessments for children and youth who present with symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
entries.notes: CNAF links to phsa.ca/our-services/programs-services/bc-autism-assessment-network, which now returns 404; the program's current page is on bcchildrens.ca (BC Children's Hospital). It is a provincial program with regional centres, so families may be assessed closer to home. A doctor's referral is needed; reports come six to eight weeks after the assessment.

entries.name: Asante FASD and Other Neurodevelopmental Services (The Asante Centre)
entries.description: A centre in Maple Ridge that assesses children, youth and adults for fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) and complex developmental and behavioural conditions, does psychoeducational assessments, and offers speech-language therapy. It does not currently do autism assessments.
entries.cost_note: Private assessments are paid by the client, family or an approved agency; some referrals come through agencies such as CLBC or Sunny Hill.
entries.address: #107 – 22335 McIntosh Avenue Maple Ridge, BC V2X 3C2
entries.evidence: Asante FASD and Other Neurodevelopmental Services offers assessments for: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD);
entries.notes: CNAF lists it under 'Places Diagnosing ASD' and links to asantecentre.org/Autism_Assessments.html (404). The site now says it does NOT currently offer Autism Spectrum Disorder assessments, and that it has re-opened its waitlist for private assessments; it is part of PLEA Community Services. Address and phone from the site footer (the email address is hidden).

entries.name: Dr. Marjolaine Limbos, Registered Psychologist
entries.description: A registered psychologist with offices in Vancouver and Coquitlam who assesses and treats children. Her autism assessments use the ADOS and ADI-R and follow the B.C. standards used for Autism Funding applications; she also helps with behaviour plans and offers therapy for children with autism and their families.
entries.cost_note: Autism assessment for a child under 4 is $2,350; therapy is $235 per 50-minute session; not covered by MSP; a sliding scale may be considered.
entries.evidence: Dr. Limbos can conduct the psychological and autism portions of the assessment and make referrals to other professionals to help ensure timely assessment.
entries.notes: CNAF links to limboschildpsychology.com/autism-assessment-vancouver, which redirects to /autism-assessment/. The site says she currently accepts autism assessments only for children aged 4 and under and screens referrals first. Second office: Unit 211 – 3030 Lincoln Ave, Coquitlam. Fees from the Fees page; contacts from the Contact page.

entries.name: WCDG Inc. and Spectrum Works Consulting (Westcoast Child Development Group)
entries.description: A Vancouver clinic of registered psychologists and a clinical counsellor that does autism and ADHD assessments and offers therapy for youth aged 16 to 18 and adults. Appointments are on site or online.
entries.cost_note: Fees are not listed; psychologists are not covered by MSP, and clients can submit receipts to extended health plans.
entries.address: 1330 West 8th Avenue, Suite 100 Vancouver, British Columbia V6H 3K2 Canada
entries.evidence: This assessment is for those who are 16 year of age or older who suspect that they may fit somewhere on the Autism Spectrum.
entries.notes: CNAF links to childdevelopmentgroup.com/index.php/assessment (403); childdevelopmentgroup.com now redirects to spectrumworks.consulting, whose About page says Westcoast Child Development Group (WCDG Inc., founded 2003) shifted from young children to youth 16-18 and adults. CNAF listed it for child autism assessments done for BCAAN; the site no longer describes child assessments.

entries.name: Disability Assistance (Persons with Disabilities designation, PWD)
entries.description: B.C. government monthly financial and health support for adults who are designated as a Person with Disabilities (PWD). Applicants must be 18 or older (they can start at 17 and a half), meet income and asset rules, and have a severe impairment expected to last more than two years that significantly restricts daily living; people already supported by CLBC or the At Home Program can use a shorter application.
entries.cost_note: A government assistance program (monthly payments and supplements).
entries.evidence: Disability assistance can help you if you need financial or health support.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old Ministry of Employment and Income Assistance page (hsd.gov.bc.ca/bcea.htm), which now redirects to the general Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction page; this is the program's current page (last updated April 10, 2025). People apply through My Self Serve or a local office.

entries.name: Music Therapy Association of BC (MTABC)
entries.description: The provincial association for music therapy in B.C. Its site explains what certified music therapists do and has a public directory for finding a certified music therapist by city; membership is open to anyone interested in music therapy.
entries.cost_note: The site does not say what music therapy costs; membership fees apply to members.
entries.evidence: Here you will find information about our organization and resources for the public, certified music therapists, and students.
entries.notes: CNAF links to mtabc.com/page.php?6, which now shows 'page not found'; the association's site is current at https://mtabc.com/ (posts dated 2026). Therapist directory: https://mtabc.com/members-directory/. Phone from the Contact page (voicemail only).

entries.name: Children and Youth with Support Needs (CYSN)
entries.description: The B.C. Ministry of Children and Family Development's services for children and youth under 19 who have, or may have, a disability or developmental delay, including family support, respite, community-based therapies and direct funding. The system is changing: families are moving to the new BC Children and Youth Disability Benefit, which is open to all eligible families from April 1, 2027.
entries.cost_note: Government program; the page describes direct funding for eligible families and free community-based services.
entries.evidence: Financial supports and services are available to help children and youth who have, or at risk of having, a disability or delay.
entries.notes: CNAF links to mcf.gov.bc.ca/spec_needs (domain gone) and to the ministry's general page; this is the program's current gov.bc.ca page (last updated October 9, 2026). Key dates on the page: Autism Funding ends March 31, 2027; the Disability Benefit is available to all eligible families from April 1, 2027; the Disability Supplement starts July 2027. Phone and email are for the CYSN Resource Line; local CYSN offices: https://gov.bc.ca/CYSNoffices.

entries.name: Autism Funding Program (AFP)
entries.description: B.C. government funding that helps families pay for eligible therapies, programs, training and equipment that support the development of a child or youth diagnosed with autism. It is being replaced by the BC Children and Youth Disability Benefit and ends on March 31, 2027.
entries.cost_note: Funding paid toward eligible services and supports; the amount depends on the child's age.
entries.evidence: Autism funding helps pay for eligible services or supports that promote skill development for children living with autism.
entries.notes: Current gov.bc.ca page (CNAF's mcf.gov.bc.ca link is gone). The page says the program continues unchanged and accepts new applications until March 2027; Autism Funding ends March 31, 2027 and families move to the Disability Benefit if eligible, so this entry will need updating then. For autism questions the page points to PAIRS (formerly Autism Information Services BC), 1-844-878-4700.

entries.name: At Home Program (AHP)
entries.description: A B.C. Ministry of Children and Family Development program for children and youth with severe disabilities and complex health care needs. It provides medical equipment, supplies and other medical benefits for eligible children.
entries.cost_note: Government program providing medical equipment and services for eligible children.
entries.evidence: The At Home Program is designed to support children and youth with severe disabilities and complex health care needs.
entries.notes: Current gov.bc.ca page (CNAF's mcf.gov.bc.ca 'Children with Special Needs' link is gone; CNAF's Ministry of Health line mentions medical equipment for children with special needs). Page last updated February 10, 2026: School-Aged Extended Therapies move to the new Disability Benefit, new families can still apply until March 2027, and Medical Benefits remain. Phone and email are for Medical Benefits.

entries.name: Indigenous Disability Canada / British Columbia Aboriginal Network on Disability Society (IDC/BCANDS)
entries.description: An Indigenous non-profit society that helps Indigenous people with disabilities and their families through disability case management, referrals and information. It helps clients get equipment, assessments and benefits such as the Disability Tax Credit, CPP Disability and British Columbia's PWD designation, and runs provincial Jordan's Principle services.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention a fee; it says it does not give funding to clients.
entries.evidence: The British Columbia Aboriginal Network on Disability Society (BCANDS) provides disability/health related support, assistance, referral, information and more, through comprehensive and coordinated individual client services.
entries.notes: CNAF links to bcands.bc.ca (now https://www.bcands.bc.ca/). The society now also calls itself Indigenous Disability Canada and describes itself as a national organisation, but its case management, PWD/MNS and Jordan's Principle programs serve B.C., so it is listed under BC; a reviewer may prefer national. Offices in Victoria and Ottawa; toll-free 1-888-815-5511.

entries.name: Aboriginal Infant Development Programs (AIDP)
entries.description: Programs across B.C. for Indigenous families of infants who have, or are at risk for, developmental delays, mainly children from birth to 3 (to 6 in some communities). Consultants make home visits, plan activities, do culturally grounded developmental and family assessments, and help families reach other services; the provincial advisor's office supports these programs.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Aboriginal Infant Development Programs in British Columbia offer support to families of infants who are at risk for or have been diagnosed with developmental delays.
entries.notes: CNAF links to aidp.bc.ca (now https://www.aidp.bc.ca/). Programs are run locally in five regions; the site's AIDP Programs page lists them. Supported by the BC Association of Aboriginal Friendship Centres and MCFD. Phone is the Office of the Advisor (FAQ page); email is the admin address on the home page.

entries.name: Community Living BC (CLBC)
entries.description: A B.C. Crown corporation that funds supports and services for adults 19 and older with a developmental disability. Through its Personalized Supports Initiative it also supports adults with autism or FASD who need significant help with daily tasks.
entries.cost_note: CLBC funds services for eligible adults; what is funded depends on how urgent the need is and the funding available.
entries.evidence: Community Living BC (CLBC) supports people in B.C. who are 19 or older who have a developmental disability.
entries.notes: Eligibility needs assessment reports and forms from an approved professional, reviewed by a CLBC facilitator at a local office. Phone and email from the Head Office page; local offices: https://www.communitylivingbc.ca/contact/local-offices/.

entries.name: Developmental Pediatrics at Sunny Hill Health Centre (BC Children's Hospital)
entries.description: BC Children's Hospital's centre for developmental assessments and rehabilitation for children and youth from across B.C. with complex medical, physical and developmental needs, including autism. Care is outpatient, with an outreach program that uses telehealth for rural and remote families.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost; patients are referred by pediatricians or specialists.
entries.evidence: We provide specialized developmental assessments and rehabilitation services to children, youth and their families from across BC.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old bcchildrens.ca Sunny Hill page (404); bcchildrens.ca/our-services/sunny-hill-health-centre now redirects to this page. Its clinics include the BC Autism Assessment Network (separate entry). The address is from the BCAAN page, which is located at Sunny Hill.

entries.name: West Coast Speech Language Pathology
entries.description: A private speech-language pathology clinic in Vancouver for all ages, with individual and group therapy for children on the autism spectrum. It offers assessments, speech, language, fluency and social skills therapy, and literacy support.
entries.cost_note: The first 30-minute consultation is free; a speech and language assessment is $960 and consultation is $192 per hour.
entries.evidence: Located in the heart of Vancouver, West Coast Speech Language Pathology is a private practice providing a wide spectrum of speech and language pathology services to all ages.
entries.notes: CNAF links to westcoastspeech.com/about-us/ (404); the clinic's site is current at https://westcoastspeech.com/. Home and school visits are possible with travel charges. Fees from the Services page.

entries.name: Columbia Speech & Language Services
entries.description: A speech-language pathology practice founded in 1987 with offices in Vancouver, Port Moody and Langley, serving the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley. It works with adults and with children, including autistic children, and offers virtual early-intervention sessions for very young children.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention fees.
entries.evidence: Columbia Speech and Language Services Inc., established in 1987, has been a trusted provider of speech-language pathology services in Vancouver, across the lower mainland and the Fraser Valley, for over three decades.
entries.notes: CNAF links to columbiaspeech.com/bio/ (404); the practice's site is current at https://columbiaspeech.com/. Other offices: 2701 Esplanade Ave, Port Moody, and 8063 199 St #340, Langley.

entries.name: City Speech Centre
entries.description: A private speech-language pathology centre in Vancouver for toddlers, teens and adults. Its therapists offer consultation, assessment and therapy for communication needs including autism, language delay, apraxia, stuttering and learning disabilities.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention fees.
entries.evidence: The speech-language pathologists at City Speech Centre provide consultation, assessment, and therapy for children and adults with a variety of speech and language issues.
entries.notes: CNAF links to cityspeechcentre.ca (two pages); that domain no longer resolves. The centre now uses https://cityspeechcentre.com/ (same Vancouver practice; Jennifer Kroeker, named by CNAF, is still listed). Phone and address from the Contact page (the email is hidden).

entries.name: FEAT BC
entries.description: A parent-founded, volunteer non-profit that has advocated since 1996 for publicly funded, science-based autism treatment for children in B.C. Its site has information on diagnosis, ABA treatment, tax deductions and court cases, and an online discussion group for parents running home ABA programs.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention fees; it asks for donations.
entries.evidence: Founded by parents who refused to settle, we provide the resources, advocacy, and community needed to ensure every child in British Columbia receives timely, science-backed treatment to reach their full potential.
entries.notes: CNAF calls it Families for Early Treatment British Columbia and links to featbc.org (now https://featbc.org/). The site has only a contact form (no phone or email). The History page says FEAT BC accepts no money from governments.

entries.name: ACT – Autism Community Training
entries.description: A B.C. non-profit that provides information, training and resources for autistic people, families, caregivers, educators and professionals, including webinars, workshops, videos and the AID Search resource portal. Its team also helps families find services and next steps in B.C., with volunteer help in several languages.
entries.cost_note: The site describes its resources, webinars and navigation help as free; some training events are paid, with discounts for free members.
entries.evidence: Autism Community Training (ACT) is a non-profit organization based in British Columbia that provides information, training, and resources for autistic people, as well as parents, caregivers, educators, and community members who support autistic individuals.
entries.notes: CNAF links to actcommunity.net, which now redirects to actcommunity.ca; CNAF also lists ACT's 'Autism Diagnosis in BC' information page under Places Diagnosing ASD (an information page, not a diagnostic service). The email address is hidden on the site. Mailing address: Sechelt, B.C.

entries.name: CBI Consultants
entries.description: A Burnaby firm, founded in 1990, that provides positive behaviour support, communication and instruction consulting for autistic and other people with disabilities and their families, plus customized employment services and training. Families pay through Autism Funding, CLBC funding or privately.
entries.cost_note: Services are paid through Autism Funding, CLBC funding or privately; current fees are available from the office.
entries.address: #204-3970 Hastings Street, Burnaby, BC, Canada V5C 6C1
entries.evidence: CBI Consultants provides technical support in the areas of communication, behaviour, and instruction.
entries.notes: CNAF links to http://www.cbiconsultants.com/ (twice); the www address no longer resolves, but the same company's site is at https://cbiconsultants.com/. The access page says it is not taking new referrals into its Children's Autism Under 6 Program and sometimes has a waitlist. It is a CLBC qualified vendor.

entries.name: PALS Autism School
entries.description: An independent special education school in New Westminster for children and teens with autism, designated by the B.C. Ministry of Education, that teaches academics, life skills and social skills using applied behaviour analysis (ABA). It runs year-round with 1:1, 2:3 or 1:3 staffing and has licensed before- and after-school care.
entries.cost_note: Tuition depends on the level of teaching support the child needs, set at the intake assessment.
entries.address: 101 Third Street New Westminster, BC V3L 2P9
entries.evidence: The school uses the proven Applied Behavioural Analysis (ABA) method to provide core education, life skills and socials skills as a foundation for independence.
entries.notes: CNAF calls it the Phoenix Academy of Learning Society; the site uses PALS Autism School / PALS Autism Society. The school is accepting applications to its waitlist. CNAF mentions an adult program, which the current site does not describe.

entries.name: Entrepreneurs with Disabilities Program (EDP) (Community Futures British Columbia)
entries.description: A federally funded program, delivered by Community Futures British Columbia, that helps people with disabilities start, maintain or grow a business in BC through business advising, coaching, short-term business skills training and support to access capital. Applicants must be 18 or older, live in BC, have a self-declared or assessed disability, and own a registered BC business or have a clear business idea.
entries.cost_note: The pages do not mention any cost.
entries.evidence: The Entrepreneurs with Disabilities Program helps entrepreneurs with disabilities start, maintain or grow a business in British Columbia.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old servicecanada.gc.ca page (now landing on the general Service Canada page); its old target, Western Economic Diversification Canada's EDP page, is archived. The program now runs through PacifiCan in BC (page dated 2026-09-18), which names Community Futures BC as the delivery partner, and through PrairiesCan in Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba (separate entries). The CFBC site says EDP is taking applications for its waitlist.
